# DeepSeek

DeepSeek is the lab with the most-quoted training cost and the most explicit statement of what
that cost leaves out. The V3 report's 2.788M H800-hours ($5.576M at $2 per hour) covers "only
the official training of DeepSeek-V3, excluding the costs associated with prior research and
ablation experiments on architectures, algorithms, or data." This chapter asks how much of the
excluded part the reports themselves let us reconstruct. Working notes with sources are in
`data/notes/deepseek.md`; 51 verbatim statements are in the claims table.

```{python}
#| echo: false
from src.chapter import *  # noqa
import numpy as np
```

## What the reports disclose of the excluded compute

The V3 report describes its ablations by size and tokens: multi-token prediction and
auxiliary-loss-free balancing each tested on a 15.7B mixture-of-experts model at 1.33T tokens and
a 228.7B model at 540 to 578B tokens, and FP8 against BF16 on models "similar to DeepSeek-V2-Lite
and DeepSeek-V2" for about 1T tokens each. Summed at 6ND with both runs of each pair counted, those disclosed ablations come to roughly
one fifth of the compute of the 3.3e24 final run (the bar below gives the exact share). Nothing about the many runs behind the
architecture and data choices is counted, so this is a floor, and a low one.

```{python}
v3 = load.runs("deepseek", "deepseek-v3"); v3 = v3[~v3["run_id"].str.contains("total-official")]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 1.8)); plots.compute_split(v3, ax=ax, title="DeepSeek-V3: disclosed ablations vs the official run (6ND FLOPs)"); plt.show()
display(Markdown(f"Disclosed non-final share for V3: **{load.experiment_share(v3):.0%}** of logged FLOPs."))
```

Two contrasts with the labs that count everything. Ai2 reports 82 percent development for Olmo
3 and Meta about 70 percent for LLaMA 1. If DeepSeek's true ratio were similar, the widely quoted
$5.6M would be a fifth to a third of the programme's compute cost.

## The one real scaling-law programme: DeepSeek LLM (2024)

The first report is the only one with a full ladder: eight IsoFLOP budgets from 1e17 to 3e20
FLOPs with about ten allocations each (roughly 80 runs, derived), fitted to
`M_opt = 0.1715 · C^0.5243` and `D_opt = 5.8316 · C^0.4757` (non-embedding FLOPs per token and
tokens), plus hyperparameter laws for learning rate and batch size. The 7B and 67B are overlaid
on the loss-versus-compute curve and described as "well-predicted" at about 1,000 times the
largest ladder run, but no numerical error is printed. Later reports (V2, V3) ablate at two fixed
scales instead of fitting laws, and R1, V3.2 and V4 mention small-scale preparation only
qualitatively. Disclosure of the experimental process has fallen with each release even as the
cost figure became more precise.

```{python}
C = np.geomspace(1e17, 5e24, 200)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.5))
D = 5.8316 * C ** 0.4757
ax.plot(C[C <= 3e20], D[C <= 3e20], color=plots.INK2, lw=2, label="Fit range (1e17 to 3e20 FLOPs)")
ax.plot(C[C >= 3e20], D[C >= 3e20], color=plots.INK2, lw=2, ls=(0, (4, 3)), label="Extrapolation")
fin = load.runs("deepseek", "deepseek-llm"); fin = fin[fin["run_id"].isin(["dsllm-7b-final", "dsllm-67b-final"])]
ax.scatter(fin["flops"], fin["tokens"], s=220, marker="*", c=plots.RUN_COLORS["final"], edgecolors=plots.SURFACE, linewidths=2, zorder=4, label="DeepSeek LLM 7B and 67B as trained (2T tokens)")
for _, r in fin.iterrows():
    ax.annotate(r["run_id"].replace("dsllm-", "").replace("-final", ""), (r["flops"], r["tokens"]), xytext=(8, -12), textcoords="offset points", fontsize=9, color=plots.INK2)
ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_yscale("log"); ax.set_xlabel("Training compute (FLOPs)"); ax.set_ylabel("Compute-optimal tokens")
ax.set_title("DeepSeek LLM data-allocation law, with the two released models"); ax.legend(loc="lower right"); plt.show()
```

Both released models sit well above the fitted optimum in tokens: they were deliberately
over-trained for inference efficiency, as most released open models are.

## Across releases: released models, one benchmark

```{python}
d = load.runs("deepseek"); d = d[d["is_final"] & d["benchmark_name"].str.contains("MMLU", na=False) & d["flops"].notna()].copy()
groups = {p: d[d["project"] == p] for p in ["deepseek-llm", "deepseek-v2", "deepseek-v3"] if (d["project"] == p).any()}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
plots.overlay_projects(groups, {k: None for k in groups}, y="benchmark_value", ax=ax, title="DeepSeek LLM to V3: MMLU (5-shot, base) vs compute")
ax.set_ylabel("MMLU 5-shot (base)")
for _, r in d.iterrows():
    ax.annotate(r["run_id"], (r["flops"], r["benchmark_value"]), xytext=(6, -10), textcoords="offset points", fontsize=8, color=plots.INK2)
plt.show()
```

## Post-training cost, stated

R1's revised report gives the RL programme's cost directly: 512 H800s for 198 hours (R1-Zero,
101K GPU-hours) plus 80 hours (R1, 41K) plus 5K for SFT data, 147K GPU-hours or $294K, about
5 percent of the V3 pretraining run. A 30B preparatory model was trained on A100s first with no
figures given. V3.2 states that post-training now exceeds 10 percent of pretraining cost.

## Narrative

**Hardware and accounting.** V3 trained on 2,048 H800s; the report gives per-stage GPU-hours
(2.664M pretraining, 119K context extension, 5K post-training). V2's report gives per-trillion-token
rates (300.6K and 172.8K GPU-hours per T tokens for the dense 67B and the MoE V2), which this
chapter uses to derive GPU-hours for the 67B and V2 finals; those rows are flagged `derived`.

**What is not reconstructable.** The compute behind architecture and data decisions for every
release after the first; any prediction error for the DeepSeek LLM law; active-parameter counts
for two V3 ablation models (flagged as guesses); GPU-hours for V4 (33T and 32T tokens, no
hours disclosed). Primary hosts were blocked from this environment; text came from DeepSeek's
GitHub-hosted PDFs and GitHub transcriptions of the arXiv papers, marked as such in the claims.
